title: REPLACE / UPSERT
description:
## REPLACE
REPLACE works like INSERT, but if a row with the same PRIMARY KEY already exists, it deletes the old row and inserts the new one.
```sql
REPLACE INTO servers (id, name, status)
VALUES (1, 'prod-1', 'upgraded');
```
If id 1 exists, it gets replaced. If not, it's inserted.

## UPSERT (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT)
UPSERT is smarter - instead of deleting and reinserting, it updates the existing row.
```sql
INSERT INTO servers (id, name, status)
VALUES (1, 'prod-1', 'upgraded')
ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET status = 'upgraded';
```
This preserves the original row and only changes what you specify.

---
## Assignment:
BWS has a config table with key-value pairs. Insert the key 'max_connections' with value '100'. If it already exists, update the value to '100'. Use UPSERT.
setupCode: CREATE TABLE config (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT); INSERT INTO config VALUES ('timeout', '30'), ('max_connections', '50'), ('debug', 'false');
runHarness: SELECT * FROM config ORDER BY key;
expectedOutput:
key | value
debug | false
max_connections | 100
timeout | 30
